⛔ A TRAP IN THE VERY TEST THE FIX MUST EDIT, WHICH THE REPORT DID NOT NAME. towerCover.test.ts:277 counts with `renderSource(file)`, NOT `codeOf(file)` — `renderSource` (:249-251) only normalises CRLF; `codeOf` (:259-261) is the one that strips comments, and it is used for the OTHER assertions (:328, :340). So the moment stinkTowerRenderer.ts joins PUBLISHERS, ANY docblock in that file that writes the literal `markTowerCover(` pushes the count to 2 and turns `.toBe(1)` RED. This repo's house style is to quote the call at the site in prose — that is exactly how a green branch turns red on merge.

THE DETERMINISM HAZARD IS FILE-SPECIFIC AND SHARPER THAN THE REPORT SAYS. The report correctly names `Bond.createdTick` vs the `ignitedAtTick` trap (towerCover.ts:196-201). What it misses: unlike towerRenderer and structureRampRenderer, `stinkTowerRenderer.sync` already has a WALL CLOCK in scope at the exact insertion point — :137 `const nowSec = performance.now() / 1000;` — used at :161 and :171-ish for cosmetic sway. An author reaching for 'a timestamp' three lines from the publish will grab the wrong one, and the test suite cannot see it (towerCover's ramp is `world.tick`-driven, towerCover.ts:82-84).

TWO FAVOURABLE FACTS THE REPORT NEVER VERIFIED, both of which make piece A safer than it argues. (a) The one-frame-lag contract holds for the stink tower: main.ts:3989 `structureRenderer.sync(world);` runs BEFORE main.ts:4031 `stinkTowerRenderer.sync(world);`, so marks made in frame N are read in N+1 exactly as towerCover.ts:35-39 requires. net_assessment: THE REPORT SURVIVES THE ATTACK ON ITS CENTRAL CLAIM AND IS UNUSUALLY WELL-SOURCED — I opened every file at every line and eleven of thirteen findings are exact, including the non-obvious one (that rampMembersAt's only `spec.` reference is `spec.shape` at structureRamp.ts:509, which is what makes the cheap reuse honest). Its headline correction of the handoff is right: hiding is not gated on RAMP_SPECS, the stink tower is genuinely the one structure in the tree with a drawn sprite and no publish site, and structureRampRenderer.ts:268 says so in a comment. USE IT. But two things must be carried into the brief or the branch will ship green over a live bug, which is this project's exact S182 failure mode. FIRST, finding 4's `still_live: false` is too strong and should not be read as 'the race/tier-9 half is closed'. `keystoneTelegraphRenderer.ts` is a fourth per-bond draw site that consumes no cover alpha, is absent from all three lists in the towerCover census, runs two lines after structureRenderer at main.ts:3991, and demonstrably re-lights faded RING connectors on nagas (Square ring) and mummies (Line ring) towers once any Dot bonds to a ring node. That is the same shape of defect as spawnerZoneRenderer — a draw site that existed and had never consumed — and it is a better answer to the owner's 'I still see connectors' than either suspect the report offered him. SECOND, finding 12's mechanism is wrong for two of its five towers: the turret and stink tower get `recipeId: null` hardcoded at healthBar.ts:364 and Helga is dropped from `towerAt` by `if (d.ehp !== null) continue;` at :363, so piece C as written repairs the three spawner towers and silently leaves the two defenders broken — a half-landing fix, which is worse than not doing it. ON THE GRADES: `four_sites_risk: NONE` is CONFIRMED and I would not soften it — I enumerated the importers myself; towerCover reaches nothing in state/, net/ or a worker, writes only module-local Sets, and PROTOCOL_VERSION legitimately stays 47. `size_estimate` is OPTIMISTIC BUT NOT WRONG in kind: 'budget Standard' is the right call, though I would price it 18-25K rather than 12-18K, because (a) the census assertion at towerCover.test.ts:277 reads RAW SOURCE INCLUDING COMMENTS, so the house style of quoting `markTowerCover(` in a docblock will turn the branch red at merge time, (b) `performance.now()` is already in scope at stinkTowerRenderer.ts:137, three lines from the insertion point, and (c) the keystone leak above is either in scope or must be written into the brief as explicitly NOT DONE. The report's own instinct — 'do ONLY the stink tower publish + its hit test + the two census edits' — is correct and should be the brief's opening line.
